Commentary.Commentary: Back for the chase. The players are out in the middle. Rohit Paudel to bowl first. Ackeem Auguste and Amir Jangoo to open for West Indies. Let's play...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Ramon Simmonds is in for a chat. He noted that the pitch had more bounce than previous games, with the ball spinning significantly. He focused on varying his pace and length to exploit these conditions.

For West Indies, Ramon Simmonds was the pick of the bowlers with his four-wicket haul! Jediah Blades supported well with 2 wickets, and Akeal Hosein and Jason Holder kept the pressure on with key breakthroughs. The West Indies bowlers have set the bar high, and now it's up to their batters to see off this target of 123! Stay tuned for the chase in a short while...

Excellent display of bowling from the West Indies side as they have managed to bundle the Nepal side of a low total of 122 runs! Nepal's innings got off to a quick start with Kushal Bhurtel's 39 off 29 balls, but regular wickets and crucial run-outs hindered their momentum. The West Indies bowlers maintained pressure, and the tail collapsed quickly, with the last five wickets falling for very little. Nepal were bowled out for 122. All in all, it was a day to forget for the Nepal batting lineup.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the game to begin. The umpires and the players are out in the middle. Kushal Malla and Kushal Bhurtel walk in with their blades for Nepal. Kyle Mayers has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

Pitch Report - Ian Bishop is at the pitchside. He says that it’s a fresh pitch with a noticeably greener surface. Adds that there’s likely to be some movement for the bowlers, and the wicket doesn’t appear as hard as the ones used in the first two games. Shares that the batters will need to work harder to build their innings, while bowlers will welcome the assistance this surface offers.

Rohit Paudel, the skipper of Nepal, says that they would have batted, so it's a good toss for them. He says that they have done well with the bat so far and they will continue to do the same. Ends by mentioning three changes on their side.

Akeal Hosein, the skipper of West Indies, says that they will bowl first as it's a fresh pitch. Adds that they will look to win this game and give their best, and avoid a clean sweep. He ends by mentioning the changes on their side.

Nepal (Playing XI) - Kushal Bhurtel, Kushal Malla, Rohit Paudel (C), Sundeep Jora, Aarif Sheikh (In for Aasif Sheikh), Gulshan Jha, Lokesh Bam (WK) (In for Dipendra Singh Airee), Mohammad Aadil Alam, Sompal Kami, Karan KC, Shahab Alam (In for Lalit Rajbanshi).

West Indies (Playing XI) - Karima Gore (In for Zishan Motara), Kyle Mayers, Keacy Carty, Ackeem Auguste, Amir Jangoo (WK), Jason Holder, Fabian Allen, Akeal Hosein (C), Navin Bidaisee, Jediah Blades, Ramon Simmonds (In for Jewel Andrew).
TOSS - West Indies have won the toss and will BOWL first.

Get ready for an electrifying contest that promises high drama! Whether it's Nepal celebrating an unprecedented whitewash or the West Indies salvaging a victory to cap off the series, the Sharjah Cricket Ground is the place to be. Toss and team news to follow shortly...

The West Indies batting lineup, which struggled severely and was bowled out for just 83 runs despite Jason Holder's top score of 21, must find its rhythm and firepower. Players like Amir Jangoo and Ackeem Auguste showed glimpses, but the collective effort needs to be vastly improved to challenge Nepal’s disciplined attack. The question remains, can the Windies put past performances behind them and deliver the explosive brand of cricket they are known for, or will Nepal continue their dream run and claim the coveted series clean sweep?

Now, all eyes are on whether the two-time T20 World Cup champions, the West Indies, can bounce back and prevent a clean sweep. Their campaign for pride starts today. Having been completely outplayed in the second game, where the formidable Nepal posted a score of 173/6, driven by impressive half-centuries from Aasif Sheikh and Sundeep Jora, the Men in Maroon will need a significant turnaround. The bowling attack will need to manage the likes of the returning Mohammad Aadil Alam, who shone with a match-winning 4 for 24, and the consistency of Kushal Bhurtel.

Welcome to the final showdown of what has been a truly historic T20 International series! The stage is set at the iconic Sharjah Cricket Ground for the third and final match between the triumphant Nepal and the determined West Indies. Nepal, or 'The Rhinos,' have already etched their names into the record books, securing their first-ever T20I series victory against a full-member nation, a remarkable achievement cemented by their commanding 90-run win in the second match.
... MATCH DAY ...

The third and final T20I between Nepal and West Indies promises to be an intriguing contest, albeit with the series already decided in Nepal's favor. Having won the first two matches convincingly, Nepal's momentum is at an all-time high, and they will look to wrap up their historic series win in style. This series marks Nepal's first-ever T20I series against a full member nation, and the significance of this achievement cannot be overstated - a win would mean the world to the team and their passionate fans. Nepal's dominance has been evident in all aspects of the game, with Sundeep Jora's impressive form posing a significant headache for the West Indies bowling unit. The Nepalese batters' ability to convert ones into twos and twos into threes has been a major plus point, and the Windies will need to curb this if they are to salvage some pride. Meanwhile, the West Indies have fielded a relatively young side, and the talent they've extracted from the CPL hasn't quite translated to the international stage, with the pressure of the occasion seemingly getting the better of them. With the weight of a key game loss on their shoulders and the series already lost, the Windies might finally unleash the brand of cricket they're known for, and it will be interesting to see if they can end the series on a high note.
